title: Requirements specification
description: Written first, from the ticket, the profile's baseline and the current behaviour. Design and testing both work from it. Every later document refers to its ids.

functional.description: Exactly one entry per acceptance criterion id given in the ticket.

id.description: The acceptance criterion id as given, e.g. AC1.

statement.description: The criterion restated so that it is testable: observable behaviour, inputs, expected result.

verified_behaviour.description: What the code or data shows today, where the ticket claims something about current behaviour.

quality.description: Non-functional requirements: those stated in the ticket, the profile baseline items that apply, and any you derive by walking the ISO/IEC 25010 product quality characteristics (e.g. performance efficiency, reliability, security, maintainability) against the change. Empty only if none apply.

id.description: NFR<n>, or the profile's own id for baseline items. Must not clash with criterion ids.

source.description: derived: proposed by you. Failures of derived requirements are reported to the user, not sent back to the implementer.

characteristic.description: ISO/IEC 25010 characteristic and sub-characteristic, e.g. 'performance efficiency / time behaviour'.

metric.description: What is measured, e.g. 'rows read per call', 'error log event with trace id'.

threshold.description: The limit. For yes/no checks use 1 for 'must hold'.

op.description: How the measured value compares to the threshold to pass. Default <=.

valid_on.description: The smallest environment where a measurement proves it. Timings at production size and real load prove only on production.

needs_design.description: True if meeting it requires a design decision (an index, a limit, a log event); the design spec must then answer it.

blocking.description: True if the answer changes scope. Blocking questions stop the run until the user answers.

functional.statement: The order history page lists every saved version of an order, newest first, and marks the version in effect when it shipped.

quality.statement: Order history reads only the versions it returns, at any history length.
quality.metric: history rows read per call for an order with 2000 versions

quality.statement: A failed history request is logged with the order id and trace id.
quality.metric: error log events with order id and trace id
